name: drawing_dimensions_itself
why: ENTRY K10, and it is the piece that closes the loop. Up to 18/9/2026 the bridge could build the part, save it, make the drawing, put three views on it, read the title block and export the PDF — and **could not put a dimension on it**. A drawing without dimensions is not a workshop drawing: it is printed geometry.
_why_CREATE_and_not_import: `model_dimensions` IMPORTS the dimensions the part already has, with `InsertModelAnnotations*`, and on this installation it brings **zero** — measured on a part with seven dimensions all marked for the drawing, on **eight** drawing templates (seven standard plus the workshop's), with five different roads, and with the positive control green in the same run (`InsertNote` on the same drawing works). That road is closed. But the aim is not «the dimensions of the model on the drawing»: it is **a dimensioned drawing**, and `AddDimension` CREATES them — out of process, four out of four. *A name that describes the means instead of the aim narrows the solutions before anyone looks for them*, and for two days the name of the other operation decided the road.
defect_caught: A dimension that **appears** and measures something else. On paper it reads the same as a right one, and in the workshop it is cut to the wrong number. That is why the case is not satisfied with `dimensions_placed`: it demands the **millimetres**, and they are those of the part — **120 the length and 10 the thickness**, the two dimensions of the outline this view shows.
_this_line_said_5_and_it_was_wrong: Up to 22/9/2026 the line above said «120 the plate, 5 the chamfer». The 5 came from a probe made on ANOTHER part, and the expectation of step 6 had already been corrected to 10 with the explanation written beside it — but this sentence had not. So the case CHECKED 10 and DECLARED 5: green every time, and whoever read it without getting to the end learned a false number. It is the defect of documents (RAG note `82c_il_difetto_che_non_da_errore_nei_documenti`) inside the file that teaches that very defect.

expect.why: the plate that is then dimensioned

steps._the_edges_are_taken_with_the_selector: The first draft used `edges_ref: { step: 1 }`, which works in the PLANS of the bridge and **not** in the declared cases: the bench answered «I do not have the geometry of that step». Two formats for the same thing, and only one valid here. With the selector the edge is named by **what it is** — X axis, 120 long, the first — instead of by where it comes from.

expect.tolerance_why: the calculation is exact (96000 minus 5*5/2*120 = 94500): the half cubic millimetre covers the rounding of SOLIDWORKS and not a fillet, which would remove 644 instead of 1500. **The first draft said 95400 — two digits swapped — and the tolerance would NOT have hidden it: a gap of 900. That is the reason it is chosen tight.**
expect.why: the chamfer serves to give the case a second measure DIFFERENT from the first: with only 120 a right dimension could not be told from a dimension that always repeats the same number. And the volume says the chamfer is really there, even before going to the drawing
a view attaches to the path of the part
the bench follows the new document (entry GT0)
the dimensions sit on the edges of a VIEW: without views there is nothing to dimension

**WHICH PART THE VIEWS ARE OF.** On 18/9/2026 a drawing came out with the views of the wrong part because no check ever asked: they counted three views and nothing else. Here we say which part, and verify that it is that one

steps._the_edges_are_named_not_counted: The first draft passed `count: 4`, and the bench raised a **bench error** on the twin: «it has not even one argument in common with the refusal, they are two operations that do not talk to each other» (entry F5). It was right. The twin asks for edge **999**: if here we said `count`, the two calls would differ by **which argument** and not by its **value** — and a pair like that does not prove that the check tells them apart, it proves that two different calls do different things. Now it is the same call with a number that exists in place of one that does not.

expect._the_seven_came_from_another_part: The first draft said SEVEN, taken from the probe of 18/9 — which however chamfered FOUR edges, while this case chamfers one. **A number measured on another geometry is not a measure of this one**, and it is the same defect as the three probes that built the part by hand (RAG note 82h): measuring an object that is not the one under examination.
expect.why: the edges are ASKED of the view, not guessed. Four is what this view shows, and if it changed, what can be dimensioned would change too
we start from zero, and it is the counterpart of «dimensions_after»: without it, four dimensions could be four dimensions that were already there

expect._said_4_and_it_was_a_repeated_dimension: Up to 23/9/2026 this expectation demanded **4**, and it passed: four edges were asked for and four dimensions were born, 120/10/120/10. That is repeated dimensioning — «each element of the object must be dimensioned no more than once» (UNI ISO 129-1, in the Sammarone sheet for Zanichelli), and the corresponding figure of the source is captioned **«therefore wrong»**. The case was green on a drawing defect: *an expectation checks what it is asked to check, not what would be right*.
expect.why: how many were BORN, counted before and after — not how many times I called the API. The value that comes back from whoever did the thing is not the measure of the thing

THE COUNTERPART OF «2». Without it, `dimensions_placed` equal to 2 would be green even if two edges had not been dimensioned because of a fault. Here we demand that the operation SAY it discarded them, and why: asking for four edges and seeing two dimensioned is surprising until you know it is a rule

the first dimension is the smallest — 10 mm, the thickness — and goes first: «the dimension lines are to be drawn in progressive order, from the smaller to the larger, moving away from the outline of the figures». On this part the smallest is the vertical one, so this expectation proves the order AND the classification together

expect._the_code_does_the_comparison: The first draft of this expectation used an operator `uguale_a_campo` to compare `contour_view_after_mm` with `contour_view_mm`. **That operator does not exist**: the evaluator of the bench compares a measure with a declared value, not two measures with each other. An expectation written with an invented operator is not a weaker expectation: it is a line the bench cannot read. The comparison was moved inside the operation, which answers «yes», «no» or «unknown» — and «unknown» when one of the two readings is missing, because a comparison that could not be made is not a comparison that went well.
expect.why: THE OUTLINE DOES NOT GROW with the dimensions attached to the view. If it grew, every following dimension would run further away than the previous one and nobody would link the two things to the placement. Measured on 23/9: [28.56, 218.55, 160.44, 240.43] before and after

**THE PART THAT MAKES THE ENTRY WORTH IT.** Not «a dimension appeared»: **what it measures**. 120 is the length of the plate, re-read by SOLIDWORKS with `GetSystemValue2` AFTER placing it — not the number I thought I had asked for. A dimension that appears and measures something else is worse than a dimension that is missing: on paper it reads the same.

expect._measured_here_and_not_elsewhere: The previous draft demanded **5**, the chamfer — taken again from the probe, where the chamfer was on four edges and showed up in that view. Here the chamfer is on ONE only and is not among the four edges of this view. Measured: `[120, 10, 120, 10]`. **The third time in a day that a number comes from a geometry different from the one under examination** — and I had already written the first two as a lesson.
expect.why: THE SECOND MEASURE, different from the first: 10 is the THICKNESS. The front view shows the 120 x 10 outline, and these are its two true dimensions. If the operation always repeated the same value, the expectation above would be green all the same and this one would not.

THE COUNTERPART, and it is the one that says **in which view** it dimensioned. 80 is the width of the plate: it is seen in the view from above, not in this one. If it appeared, the operation would have dimensioned **another view** — and the two expectations above would be green all the same, because there too there is a 120. Without this line, «contains 120» does not say where.

expect._the_root_not_the_whole_word: This expectation looked for the root «accavall», not the whole word (measured on 23/9: «accavallano» -> «si accavalla»). On 26/9 the text stopped conjugating it and cites the name of the field, «overlapping_texts»: window 2 translated that quotation, and with it the Italian root. The name cited is today the most stable proof: it is what the code writes literally.
expect.why: the blindness travels with the answer: the operation puts RIGHT dimensions, not a NICE drawing, and does not look at whether they overlap the drawing. Whoever reads this answer may not have read the catalogue

ENTRY Z-A2, THE GREEN ON A REAL CASE: two dimensions just placed on edges that the view shows, and the state re-read from scratch says they are attached. The red — the dimension that is left without an edge when the part changes — is proved by the C# group «orphans», because a declared case cannot go back to the part after opening the drawing. Zero here is an assertion: null would mean «I do not know» (entry Z-C8)
